title: RF-DETR vs YOLOv9: 58.6 vs 57.1 mAP, YOLOv9 22.8% faster
dek: YOLOv9 wins the small end and runs 22.8% faster at matched size on an RTX 5070 Ti. RF-DETR-L tops out at 58.6 mAP, YOLOv9-C at 57.1.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: Neither family wins outright on an RTX 5070 Ti. YOLOv9 leads at the small end and runs 22.8% faster on average in PyTorch; RF-DETR leads at the large end, where RF-DETR-L reaches 58.6 mAP against YOLOv9-C at 57.1. Across 4 nearest-parameter pairs the accuracy split is 2 to 2, with YOLOv9 averaging 1.5 mAP points higher.

RF-DETR fields 4 measured variants; YOLOv9 fields 4. All run the same COCO val2017 protocol on an RTX 5070 Ti. RF-DETR's variants sit between 30.47M and 33.93M parameters, so each pairs with YOLOv9-C (25.5M) by count.

blocks.caption: Accuracy vs parameters on COCO val2017. Every RF-DETR and YOLOv9 variant highlighted against the full set.

blocks.text: mAP is shown in percent. Against YOLOv9-C at 57.1 mAP, RF-DETR-N trails at 51.4 and RF-DETR-S at 55.1. RF-DETR-M leads by 0.2 points at 57.3 and RF-DETR-L by 1.5 at 58.6. That is a 2 to 2 split, with YOLOv9 ahead by 1.5 points on average. At the small end YOLOv9-T reaches 41.8 mAP at 2.04M parameters, a size class RF-DETR does not field.
YOLOv9 is faster at matched compute: 22.8% faster on average in PyTorch FP32. YOLOv9-C runs 42.3 FPS; RF-DETR runs 39.5 FPS at RF-DETR-N and 25.1 FPS at RF-DETR-L.

The accuracy lead changes hands with model size. At the small end YOLOv9 leads: its parameter-efficient variants sit above RF-DETR's smallest, RF-DETR-N, which needs 30.47M parameters to reach 51.4 mAP. At the large end RF-DETR leads, with RF-DETR-L at 58.6 mAP. There is no single winner; the choice follows your size class.

items.v: Both families ship under permissive licenses

blocks.text: Pick YOLOv9 for small and mid-size deployments and for throughput: it fields models from 2.04M parameters and is faster at matched size. Pick RF-DETR-L when peak accuracy matters more than frame rate: it reaches 58.6 mAP, 1.5 points above YOLOv9-C, at 25.1 vs 42.3 FPS. Both ship under permissive licenses. See the per-variant specs on the RF-DETR and YOLOv9 model pages.
